appraisal_events.evidence: elle se plaignit que ce fût en effet bien tard... elle ne le garderait pas plus d'une demi-heure, qu'à minuit, elle le renverrait; and to his hopeful "pas de catleyas ce soir?" she answers, "d'un air un peu boudeur et nerveux": "Mais non, mon petit, pas de catleyas ce soir, tu vois bien que je suis souffrante!"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator sets up Swann's complacent certainty that Odette was reserving the evening for him, then shows that certainty undercut: she treats his arrival as an inconvenience, strictly limits his time, and flatly refuses the intimacy he had hoped for, citing illness in an irritated tone.

status_effects.explanation: Swann arrives hoping for the intimacy he has come to prize above all else and is instead rebuffed and given only a curtailed, bounded visit.
Odette dictates the terms of the encounter and withholds what Swann wants, locally exercising leverage over him.

ambiguities: The passage's opening account of Swann's reasoning (his confident sense that the evening was secured for him, and his half-formed thought of not coming at all) is narrated with irony that the ensuing rebuff exposes; this framing affects whether the snub reads as narrator-endorsed or merely reported.
